answer: At the nadir of a Sybil flood, each new agent must present a cryptographic proof that its identity shares a vault key with an existing node, linking payment timestamps to a reef of prior transactions. The network aggregates these links into a weighted graph and only promotes a node to summit status when its cumulative stake and timing pattern exceed a dynamic threshold. An attacker must acquire multiple funded accounts, synchronize their spending cycles and forge vault signatures, raising the cost to dozens of dollars per fake node.
